properties.name: Beirut
properties.role: Coastal terminus (Mar Mikhael); rack climb begins
properties.description: Beirut’s first railway station and the coastal terminus of the 1895 Beirut–Damascus line — the first significant railway in the Levant, pre-dating the Hejaz Railway by 13 years. The station building (completed 1893 by the Société de construction des Batignolles on the PLM model, adapted to the local climate — an encircling marquise, taller ceilings, a triple-arched central window) stood just beyond the old city by the port, linked to the Hamidiyeh souk (today Martyrs’ Square) along the Tripoli road (now Rue d’Arménie). It was the hub of both the Beirut–Damascus railway and the Tramway Libanais, and from 1903 connected onward to La Gare du Port. Regular passenger service ended with the civil war; the ~62,000 m² site survived as the railway authority’s (OFTC/OCFTC) headquarters and, after the 2020 port explosion that damaged it, became the subject of an Italy/UNESCO/UN-Habitat heritage-and-public-space revival.
